citations.claim: EW was green at step 122 just before emergency
EW cut to yellow for only 1s at step 123 when emergency went active
NS turned green at step 124 with 0s all-red, violating clearance

counterfactual.change: Removed the single emergency event (S at t=123); otherwise identical, same 124 steps. Emergency preemption is what truncates yellow and skips all-red, so without it the cycle runs full yellow and all-red and no violation occurs.

explanation: Emergency preemption immediately forces the emergency direction green: EW green at step 122 goes to EW yellow for a single second at step 123 (instead of 6s yellow) then directly to NS green at step 124 with 0s all-red (instead of 2s). The controller's emergency override bypasses the normal yellow-duration and all-red clearance timers, causing all_red_clearance (and yellow_duration) violations.

violation.detail: approach 0 turned green after only 0 s of all-red (need 2 s)

vision_note: The east-west approaches show green in steps 121-122 and switch to yellow in step 123, then the north-south approaches are already green in step 124. There is only one second of yellow with no intervening all-red step where all approaches are red.
